# Powers of Two — Doubling and Binary Place Value

## The identity to remember

$$
2^k=1+\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}2^i
$$

**Every symbol explained:** k is a positive integer; 2^k is the kth power of two; Σ adds all lower powers from exponent i=0 through k−1.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For k=4, 2⁴=16 and 1+(1+2+4+8)=16. The lower powers alone sum to 15.

## Why it is true

From the geometric series, 1+2+⋯+2^(k−1)=2^k−1. Add one to both sides to get the identity.

## Algorithm or number puzzle application

Recognise binary place values, complete binary trees, power-of-two buffers and overflow thresholds.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

An unsigned 4-bit integer stores 0 through 2⁴−1=15. It has 16 different bit patterns.

## Your turn

The number 2^k is not itself representable in only k unsigned bits. Signed representation has a different usable range.

**Memory rule:** Remember the mathematical structure behind the bit or counting operation, not a memorised code template.
